# Building AI Agents and Advanced AI Workflows

## Overview
The frontier of automation right now is AI agents - workflows where the AI does not just answer once but can reason, choose actions, and use tools to accomplish a goal - and beginner-friendly tools now make this buildable without deep ML knowledge. A single AI call (Day 26) takes input and returns output. An AI agent goes further: given a task, it can decide which 'tools' to use, in what order, and loop until the job is done. Tools are just capabilities you give the agent - search a database, call an API, send an email, look something up - exposed via 'function calling', where the model outputs which tool to run and with what inputs, your workflow executes it, and the result goes back to the agent to continue reasoning. For example, an agent handling a customer question might look up the order in your database, check a policy document, and draft a reply - choosing those steps itself. n8n has a dedicated AI Agent node and Make has AI features that make wiring this up approachable, letting you connect a model to tools you define. You will also meet RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) at a basic level: instead of hoping the model already knows your company's specifics, you retrieve relevant documents (from a knowledge base or vector store) and feed them as context so answers are grounded and accurate. Crucially, agents need guardrails: validate their outputs, limit which actions they can take, cap costs and loops, and keep a human in the loop for risky decisions - because an unconstrained agent can make expensive or wrong choices. Being able to build a safe, useful, tool-using AI agent is a cutting-edge, highly marketable skill that builds directly on everything you have learned.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: AI agents vs single AI calls; Tools/function calling (letting AI take actions); n8n AI Agent node and Make AI features; Retrieval and giving AI context (RAG basics); Guardrails, validation, and human-in-the-loop. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: In n8n (or Make), build a simple AI agent that is given one or two tools (e.g., a database lookup and a send-message action) and can answer a request by choosing and using the right tool, returning a final response.
Mini Project: Build an AI customer-assistant agent: it receives a question, retrieves relevant info from a knowledge base or database (basic RAG), decides whether it can answer or must escalate, drafts a grounded reply, and routes anything uncertain to a human for approval.
Assignment: Explain the difference between a single AI call and an AI agent, describe what 'tools/function calling' enables, and list three guardrails you would put on an agent that can send emails.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.

## Next Steps After Today
- Complete the practical task and submit it for AI review.
- Read any research papers linked for deeper theory.
- Prepare questions for tomorrow's module.

## Resources
- Use the linked videos and documentation as reference material.
- Read the research papers for theoretical depth.
- Check the GitHub repositories for working code examples.

## Assessment
After finishing the work, open the AI Assessment popup to submit your practical results. DeepSeek will evaluate your submission, calculate a dynamic score based on correctness and depth, and add the points to your CalibiAI profile.
